title: Redbelly and Quant Overledger: interoperability feasibility

statusKey.confirmed: Stated in a public source that is linked next to the claim.

sources.title: The Clearing House Partners with Quant to Advance the On-Chain Money Initiative
sources.supports: TCH selected Quant to power the On-Chain Money Initiative, a network for clearing and settling tokenised deposits, connected to RTP and CHIPS and expected to be available to participating institutions in the first half of 2027.

sources.title: The Clearing House Partners with Quant to Advance the On-Chain Money Initiative (Quant press release)
sources.supports: Quant's technology provides the network's interoperability, orchestration and transaction-management layer; Quant also offers Tokenised Deposits-as-a-Service to institutions that process through TCH but lack tokenised deposit capability.

sources.title: Quant powers The Clearing House's On-Chain Money Initiative in the US
sources.supports: Quant describes its role as coordinating clearing and settlement of tokenised deposit transactions with connectivity to existing fiat payment systems.

sources.title: Major Financial Institutions Unveil Bank-Led On-Chain Money Initiative
sources.supports: The initiative was unveiled in June 2026 as a bank-led effort, operated by TCH, for on-chain clearing and settlement of tokenised deposits between banks.

sources.title: Start Here (Overledger documentation)
sources.supports: Overledger is Quant's multi-DLT platform for applications that span more than one blockchain, with one set of credentials and one API surface; client integrations start with the Gateway and Connectors chapters.

sources.title: Overview (Overledger documentation)
sources.supports: The Gateway handles authentication, routing to Connectors or the Fusion Rollup, rate limiting, observability and orchestration of Flow Applications; a Cross Chain Messaging component moves data and contract calls between connected networks; Fusion Firewall policies are mirrored on each connected L1.

sources.title: Connectors (Overledger documentation)
sources.supports: Connectors present a single multi-DLT RPC endpoint backed by per-family node pools; six self-serve families (EVM, Solana, Cosmos, SUI, Hedera, Aptos); permissioned and consortium networks need a managed engagement; a first POST /nodes call can register a new network in a supported family; public nodes only from whitelisted providers, private nodes from any domain; administrative RPC methods are blocked; live list via GET /networks.

sources.title: Authentication (Overledger documentation)
sources.supports: Users sign in to Quant Connect for a JWT, mint API keys through the REST API and send them with RPC calls; API keys authenticate access but transactions still need the caller's own wallet signature.

sources.title: Signing (Overledger documentation)
sources.supports: A Signer Flow App handles signing: either the client holds keys and signs, or Quant holds them (testnet hot wallet, or contracted mainnet KMS or HSM); the Gateway and calling Flow App never see private keys.

sources.title: Overledger Firewall (Overledger documentation)
sources.supports: An off-chain Connector layer decides whether an authenticated user may reach a network (permissioned networks need the user on an allowlist); an on-chain Fusion Firewall allowlists addresses for contract calls, cross-chain messages and token bridging.

sources.title: Fusion Rollup (Overledger documentation)
sources.supports: Fusion is a multi-ledger optimistic rollup (an OP Stack fork) that anchors to several L1s at once; primitives cover deposit, unify, trigger and withdraw or mint; at testnet launch it connected Ethereum Sepolia, Polygon Amoy and a Quant permissioned Besu testnet; the firewall is locked down on mainnet and more permissive on testnet; a sender on a connected network must be allowlisted for the specific rollup recipient; it flags lock-and-mint mismatch, custodian compromise and oracle failure as bridge risks.

sources.title: How to create a bridge flow (Overledger documentation)
sources.supports: Bridges are created through a bridge flow in Quant Connect that deploys a destination token contract and returns a Bridge ID used for transfers.

sources.title: Overledger API reference
sources.supports: Quant publishes a reference for the Overledger APIs, the interface any connection would be built against.

sources.title: Manage Webhooks for Smart Contract Events (Overledger documentation)
sources.supports: Overledger documents webhooks that notify applications about smart contract events.

sources.title: Redbelly Network Technical Documentation
sources.supports: Redbelly describes itself as a layer 1 blockchain built and optimised for real world asset tokenisation, with identity and eligibility tooling for developers.

sources.title: Receptor (Redbelly documentation)
sources.supports: Receptor is Redbelly's native identity and verifiable credential protocol, built on the W3C verifiable credential data model, with Issuer, Holder and Verifier modules; anyone can issue credentials, but issuers that provide network access are accredited.

sources.title: Issuer module (Redbelly documentation)
sources.supports: Only accredited issuers can issue credentials that give users network access.

sources.title: Proof by Query (Redbelly documentation)
sources.supports: Proof by Query uses zero-knowledge proofs checked by a verifier smart contract that the verifier deploys on Redbelly Network (setZKPRequest), to which the holder submits a proof (submitZKPResponse); personal data is not seen or stored by the verifier.

sources.title: Selective Disclosure (Redbelly documentation)
sources.supports: Selective Disclosure verifies credentials that require users to reveal specified, verifiable information off-chain.

sources.title: Eligibility SDK: Getting Started (Redbelly documentation)
sources.supports: The Eligibility SDK is installed as @redbellynetwork/eligibility-sdk and needs a Redbelly API key and an allowed issuer DID.

sources.title: Configure Eligibility Criteria (Redbelly documentation)
sources.supports: Eligibility criteria are Iden3-style queries over credential types such as passport, proof of address and AML/CTF credentials; on-chain checks use the credentialAtomicQuerySigV2OnChain circuit; on-chain single queries are supported, multi-query is planned.

sources.title: Redbelly Network environments (Vine developer portal)
sources.supports: Mainnet is chain ID 151 with RBNT as currency and a public RPC URL; Testnet is chain ID 153.

sources.title: DBFT and super block: security, finality and scalability (Vine developer portal)
sources.supports: Security, finality and scalability come from DBFT, a leaderless consensus algorithm tolerating faults up to t < n/3, and the super block optimisation of the EVM.

sources.title: Smart contracts (Vine developer portal)
sources.supports: Redbelly executes smart contracts written for the EVM in Solidity; testing should happen on Testnet.

sources.title: Network fees (Vine developer portal)
sources.supports: The unit price of gas is fixed in US dollar terms and converted to RBNT at execution using an on-chain price oracle.

sources.title: Redbelly Network native currency (Vine developer portal)
sources.supports: Lists routes for RBNT on other chains (Base via LayerZero, Ethereum mainnet via Polymer) and points to Lucid Labs Bridge for moving RBNT back to Redbelly.

sources.title: Accessing the network (Vine developer portal)
sources.supports: Users connect an EVM wallet to the Redbelly access dApp and prove a valid photo identity document through biometric checks before their account is enabled.

sources.title: Redbelly Access
sources.supports: Identity is verified by the accredited issuer Averer before it issues the Redbelly Network Access Credential to the account.

sources.title: Redbelly DevNet blog post
sources.supports: Before users can self-enable their accounts with write access to the network, they must claim an access credential from a network accredited issuer.

sources.title: Node operator guide (Vine developer portal)
sources.supports: Companies or trusts may register through Redbelly's Business verification process.

sources.title: Tokeniser
sources.supports: Tokeniser operates on Redbelly Network with identity and eligibility built into the protocol; eligibility (identity, KYC, AML, CTF, wholesale and sophisticated investor tests, TMD) is programmed into every asset; every holder is verified and every transfer checked against the asset's rules; features include secondary transfer and collateral mobility.
excerpts: every transfer checked against the asset's rules

sources.title: Celer Announces cBridge Support for Redbelly
sources.supports: cBridge connects Ethereum, BNB Chain and Redbelly with a pegged bridge model; RBNT moves from Redbelly to Ethereum and BNB Chain.

sources.title: Redbelly Network on X: Wrapped RBNT live on Ethereum Mainnet
sources.supports: Redbelly announced Wrapped RBNT on Ethereum Mainnet with the official contract 0xb45ffb51984d626ee758b336c61cf20990c6bf13.
sources.manual: x.com serves this post through JavaScript, so automated fetches often fail. Open it in a browser to confirm.

sources.title: Deployed Endpoints, Message Libraries, and Executors (LayerZero V2)
sources.supports: Redbelly Mainnet is listed among LayerZero V2 deployments.

sources.title: TASK-08 Existing Bridge Integration Guide (winning entry archive)
sources.supports: A working lock-and-mint bridge from Ethereum Sepolia to Redbelly Testnet (chain ID 153) secured by a 2-of-3 relayer set, plus research on which bridge protocols support Redbelly.

sources.title: redbelly-testnet-bridge (ARTICLE.md)
sources.supports: Every wallet needs identity verification before it can send any Testnet transaction; unverified deploys fail with 'Sender not authorised to write transactions'; Mainnet and Testnet approvals are separate.
excerpts: Sender not authorised to write transactions
Mainnet and Testnet approvals are separate

sources.title: TASK-16 Unstick Your RBNT: Cross-Chain Recovery Playbook (winning entry archive)
sources.supports: Recovery steps for stuck cross-chain RBNT, including that transfers bridged to Ethereum via Polymer do not relay automatically, and that only the Ethereum wRBNT contract has been officially announced.

sources.title: TASK-29 Quant Overledger and Redbelly Interoperability Research (task brief)
sources.supports: Redbelly and Quant have no announced partnership or talks; Redbelly has not published an official position on bridging.
